definition: Predicting which image regions attract human attention, outputting a saliency map.
details: Predicting which image regions attract human attention, outputting a saliency map. It supports cropping, compression, and studying visual attention.

explainer.lead: Saliency detection predicts which image regions attract human attention, producing a saliency map. It matters because it supports cropping, compression, and the study of visual attention.

tiers.eli5: It works out which parts of a picture a person would look at first.
tiers.practitioner: Used to guide cropping and compression by prioritising high-saliency regions; the output is a dense saliency map rather than a single label.
tiers.paperLevel: The task of predicting which image regions attract human attention and outputting a saliency map. Limits: it predicts attention rather than measuring it directly.

explainer.example: Saliency detection on a photo yields a saliency map highlighting the regions most likely to draw attention, which then guides a crop.
